newsitem.title: JAPAN: Foreigners have record holdings in Japan stocks.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners have record holdings in Japan stocks.

text.p: Despite their lacklustre performance in the face of a prolonged economic slump, Japan's stock markets are enjoying record-high holdings by foreign investors.

The National Conference of Stock Exchanges, a research body for Japan's eight stock exchanges, said on Thursday that as of the end of March, foreign investors owned 9.8 percent of all the outstanding shares in Japan. The numbers were based on holdings among 2,339 listed companies.
The proportion of foreign shareholdings is a rise of 0.4 percentage points from the same time last year and the seventh-straight year showing an increase.
At the same time, the foreigners -- along with domestic investors -- have seen a drop in the value of their holdings.

The survey showed that foreign investors held 40 trillion yen ($353 billion) worth of stocks based on market value at the end of the financial year on March 31, down by 800 billion yen ($7.07 billion) from a year earlier.
The proportion of Japanese stocks held by individual investors was 23.6 percent at the end of March, unchanged from a year earlier, the survey showed.
But the number of individual shareholders totalled 27.37 million at the end of March, up 330,000 from a year earlier, marking the first rise in three years.
